extracted.intended_audience: registered USPTO practitioners (patent attorneys and agents), OED staff, counsel in practitioner discipline/reinstatement matters
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and substantive standards under 37 C.F.R. § 11.29 for reciprocally transferring a practitioner to disability inactive status based on a transfer in another jurisdiction, including the required notices, available defenses, burdens of proof, and effects/rehabilitation procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notification to OED Director (37 C.F.R. § 11.29(a)(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: Within thirty days of being transferred to disability inactive status in another jurisdiction, a practitioner shall notify the OED Director.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Upon notification the OED Director shall obtain a certified copy of the order transferring the practitioner to disability inactive status in the other jurisdiction and file with the USPTO Director: the order; a request that the practitioner be transferred to disability inactive status (including specific grounds); and a request that the USPTO Director issue a Notice and Order. (37 C.F.R. § 11.29(a)(1)(i)-(iii)).

rubrics_metrics.name: USPTO Notice and Practitioner Response (37 C.F.R. § 11.29(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: After receiving the OED Director's submission, the USPTO Director provides a Notice and Order directing the practitioner to respond within 30 days, providing all evidence that would establish a genuine issue of material fact as to the factors set forth in 37 C.F.R. § 11.29(d).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The practitioner may file a response and the OED Director may reply; the Director considers timely filings before imposing the identical transfer unless the practitioner meets one of the defenses by clear and convincing evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Burden and Standard of Proof — clear and convincing
rubrics_metrics.description: The USPTO Director shall impose the identical transfer to disability inactive status based on the practitioner's transfer in another jurisdiction unless the practitioner demonstrates by clear and convincing evidence (or the Director finds by clear and convincing evidence) a genuine issue of material fact as to one of the defenses in § 11.29(d).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The burden to prove a genuine issue of material fact on the § 11.29(d) factors lies with the practitioner. Misstatements by a practitioner that the OED must meet this burden are incorrect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Due Process Defense (37 C.F.R. § 11.29(d)(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: A practitioner may defeat a reciprocal transfer by clearly and convincingly demonstrating that the state proceeding was so lacking in notice or opportunity to be heard as to constitute a deprivation of due process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Due process requires the opportunity to be heard at a meaningful time and in a meaningful manner (Mathews v. Eldridge). Satisfied where respondent had reasonable notice, was represented by counsel, participated, could present evidence, testify, call and cross-examine witnesses, and make objections and arguments. Case law: In re Karten; In re Squire; In re Zdravkovich; In re Feng Li; In re Brufsky; In re Ruffalo; In re Cook.

rubrics_metrics.name: Infirmity of Proof Defense (37 C.F.R. § 11.29(d)(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: A practitioner may defeat reciprocal transfer by showing by clear and convincing evidence that there was such an infirmity of proof establishing the transfer to disability status (judicial declaration, involuntary commitment, guardianship/conservatorship) that the USPTO Director could not accept the conclusion as final.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a difficult showing to make, particularly where the practitioner voluntarily consented to the underlying state action (consent/voluntary resignation does not generally support infirmity of proof). Case citations: In re Zdravkovich; In re Day; In re Lebowitz; In re Haley. Practitioner's failure to contest the state proceeding undermines this defense.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grave Injustice Defense (37 C.F.R. § 11.29(d)(3))
rubrics_metrics.description: A practitioner may defeat reciprocal transfer by showing by clear and convincing evidence that imposition of the same disability status by the USPTO Director would result in grave injustice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Arguments such as differentiating patent agent vs patent attorney status are insufficient because USPTO regulations treat agents and attorneys equally for disciplinary/jurisdictional purposes. Practitioner must produce clear and convincing evidence of grave injustice; absent such proof, reciprocal transfer is appropriate. Practitioner may seek reinstatement to address fitness concerns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identity Defense (37 C.F.R. § 11.29(d)(4))
rubrics_metrics.description: A practitioner may avoid reciprocal transfer by proving that the practitioner is not the individual who was transferred to disability status, judicially declared incompetent, involuntarily committed, or placed under guardianship/conservatorship.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If practitioner concedes identity (as in this case), this defense will not be considered. The burden to show non-identity is by clear and convincing evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Independent Grounds for Transfer (37 C.F.R. § 11.19(b)(2)(i)-(iii))
rubrics_metrics.description: Transfer to disability inactive status before the USPTO may be based on various grounds, including being transferred to disability inactive status in another jurisdiction, judicial declaration of incompetence, or judicial involuntary commitment/guardianship/conservatorship.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Being transferred to disability inactive status in another jurisdiction is an independent and sufficient basis for reciprocal transfer under § 11.29(d); other paths (judicial finding of incompetence, etc.) exist but are not required where § 11.19(b)(2)(i) applies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinction Between Disciplinary Action and Disability Transfer
rubrics_metrics.description: The process and grounds for disciplinary action (suspension/exclusion for incompetence, disreputable conduct, gross misconduct) differ from the processes/grounds for transfer to disability inactive status.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disciplinary provisions (e.g., 37 C.F.R. § 11.19(b)(1)(i)-(v)) may require findings of incompetence or disreputable conduct; the disability-transfer provision (37 C.F.R. § 11.19(b)(2)(i)) does not require such findings. The two processes are separate and distinct.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effects and Duties Upon Transfer
rubrics_metrics.description: Once transferred to disability inactive status by the USPTO, the practitioner is precluded from practicing before the USPTO in patent, trademark, and other non-patent matters until further order of the USPTO Director.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Orderable consequences include: publication of a Notice in the Official Gazette; notice to disciplinary enforcement agencies, courts, and the public (per 37 C.F.R. §§ 11.29(h)(2) and 11.59); practitioner must comply with duties enumerated in 37 C.F.R. § 11.58; USPTO will dissociate practitioner's name from Customer Numbers and PKI certificates; practitioner may not apply for or be added to a Customer Number until reinstated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reinstatement Process and Proof of Fitness (37 C.F.R. §§ 11.29(j), 11.58, 11.60)
rubrics_metrics.description: A practitioner transferred to disability inactive status may immediately seek reinstatement under the cited provisions and, in any reinstatement petition, has the opportunity to demonstrate fitness to practice before the Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State rules (e.g., Michigan MCR 9.121(E)) may require a showing by clear and convincing evidence that the attorney's disability has been removed and that he/she is fit to resume practice; analogous proof will be considered by the USPTO in reinstatement proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evidence Types and Weight (state order, stipulation, medical records)
rubrics_metrics.description: Proof supporting a reciprocal transfer includes a certified copy of the state order transferring the practitioner to disability inactive status, any stipulation/consent entered in state proceedings, and medical evidence (e.g., stroke resulting in aphasia) demonstrating incapacity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consent/stipulation to transfer and clear medical documentation weigh heavily and make infirmity-of-proof defenses difficult; an uncontested factual record (e.g., certified state order and supporting documents) is sufficient basis for reciprocal transfer unless practitioner produces clear and convincing contrary evidence.
